snapshot: Capture the logical credential revision and sent access/refresh pair. Re-reading unexpected external credentials or a token storage event changes the revision. Own confirmed refresh rotation alone preserves it. No JWT claim grants client authority.
refresh: One promise bound to source revision+pair; all consumers await the same success/rejection; finally clears only its own job. Old-job finalization cannot release a newer account job.
boundaries: After JSON/Blob body and PDF signature reads
Before exposing a response or creating a PDF download
late_old_401: Abort with session_changed before starting any refresh or resend under a new account.
late_old_refresh: Preserve newer credentials and reject all old waiters before saving its response.
known_same_session_rotation: A late401 from an older request retries the currently known own-rotated pair without a second refresh. Its original payload and idempotency key remain unchanged.
definitive_failure: The existing expired-session flow may clear and redirect only while the exact failed pair/revision remains current; changed credentials are preserved.
public_auth: loginGym/loginUsuario/registro send neither Bearer nor automatic refresh on401; a successful delayed login cannot replace a changed logical session. Explicit saveTokens marks a new revision. Logout never clears a newer revision.
blob_transports: PDF and private logo use the same authenticated fetch path as JSON. Their existing validation and URL cleanup remain in effect.
storage_limit: Two legacy keys and direct writers mean snapshot checks are not a full cross-tab atomic transaction. This follow-up does not close R10 or all session races.
